title: The finite dualizing counit comparison commutes with mixed quotients
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D, a prime l≠D.p, finite extensions E,L of Q_l and an embedding iota:E→L. Let X be a separated finite-type D.k-scheme and n≤m. Use the finite dualizing terms and exceptional transitions t_F of [def-coef-finite-dualizing-data], the counit-defined cross-field maps finiteU of [def-sf-integral-finite-extension-models], and the mixed scalar/quotient mate a of [def-sf-scalar-reduction-exchange]. Then T_(iota_m)(t_E);a_(omega_(E,n));Res_L(finiteU_n)=finiteU_m;t_L. No integral dualizing datum or choice of integral lift is used.

proof.text: The two coefficient paths agree on residue representatives. Paste the proper coefficient counit mates and the open balancing squares; their outer compact-support comparisons agree by functoriality and associativity. The two regular coefficient unit maps agree because they send 1 to 1. One can check on a larger ramification-multiple quotient and then descend by the quotient comparison cocycle.

Transpose this equality under the exceptional and scalar adjunctions. The resulting maps are exactly finiteEtaleU and the finite dualizing transition. Transport through the scalar-section-normalized realization restriction squares and the origins; their inverse pairs cancel. Identity-on-sections coherence identifies the mixed map with scalarReductionExchange. This yields the asserted equality for all target exponents, including m=n and exponent one.

theorem finiteU_quotient_transition {m n : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m) :
    (pbcDerivedExtend (integralScalarQuotientSheafMap l E L ι X m)).map
        (integralDualizingExceptionalTransition l E D X hl h) ≫
      (scalarReductionExchange l E L ι X h).app (integralDualizingFiniteTerm l E D X n) ≫
      (normalizedDVRRes l L X h).map (finiteU l E L ι X D n) =
    finiteU l E L ι X D m ≫ integralDualizingExceptionalTransition l L D X hl h
